title: Re-dragging an item the frame it's dropped causes the item to misalign
line: Desktop icons dragged with a quick flick, or grabbed again right after a drop, now stay under the pointer and land where you drop them.
explanation: Folder View anchors the drag image to the pointer position at the moment the drag actually starts, not where the icon was pressed. A drag only starts after the drag distance is crossed and, since the 6.8.3 fix, after the drag image is ready, so with a fast flick or a quick re-grab the pointer has already travelled tens of pixels by then; the icon is drawn that far behind the pointer and is dropped at that offset. The change passes the press position to dragSelected(), so the icon keeps the offset it had when it was grabbed.

commits.message:
containments/desktop: anchor the drag image where the icon was pressed

The drag hotspot used the pointer position at the moment the drag began,
so if the pointer moved quickly before that, the icon was dragged away
from the pointer and dropped there. Use the press position instead.

BUG: 527529

media.caption: Master: an unselected icon pressed and flicked away in one motion; the icon trails far behind the pointer and lands away from it (slowed 2x).
With the fix: the same flick keeps the icon under the pointer, and it lands where it is dropped (slowed 2x).
Master: icon dropped and grabbed again 30 ms later; the pointer sits at a different spot on the icon each drag and the drop lands a row off (slowed 2x).
With the fix: both drags hold the icon where it was grabbed and it lands under the pointer (slowed 2x).

review.text: Passing (pressX, pressY) instead of (mouse.x, mouse.y) to dir.dragSelected() directly fixes the hotspot and drop-offset misalignment caused by fast flicks or quick re-drags while the drag threshold or async drag-image generation delays drag start. Both coordinate pairs are in the same MouseEventListener space, so anchoring to the press point keeps the dragged icon under the pointer and drops it in the expected cell without regressing multi-selection or normal drags. The before/after recordings clearly confirm both the fast-flick and immediate re-drag cases.

reviews.text: Passing (pressX, pressY) instead of (mouse.x, mouse.y) to dir.dragSelected() directly fixes the hotspot and drop-offset misalignment caused by fast flicks or quick re-drags while the drag threshold or async drag-image generation delays drag start. Both coordinate pairs are in the same MouseEventListener space, so anchoring to the press point keeps the dragged icon under the pointer and drops it in the expected cell without regressing multi-selection or normal drags. The before/after recordings clearly confirm both the fast-flick and immediate re-drag cases.

Using the press position as the drag hotspot is the standard, correct approach (pressX/pressY are in the same MouseArea space as mouse.x/y and are only cleared after the call), and it addresses the remaining offset that cwo's drag-image fix made more likely by deferring drag start. Both reporter scenarios (re-grab right after a drop, click+drag in one motion) are shown fixed in the videos; frames confirm the pointer stays at the grab point and the icon lands under it. One-line, low-risk change; commit message and explanation match the patch.
